A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReDDiT research. Their text, equations, figures and tables are readable, including v3 Appendices A-G. v1 ends with references and has no separate appendix. Relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, component and sampling ablations, and qualitative generation and inpainting results in Tables 1-3 and Figures 3-7.

after.justification: v3 retains original ImageNet experiments and adds quantitative sampler comparisons and cache acceleration results in Appendix D/Figure 7 and Appendix F/Table 5.

M1.justification: Appendix F introduces optional dLLM-Cache adaptation, updating response keys and values every two or four decoding steps while disabling prompt caching. The core corruption process, objective and rehash sampler remain unchanged. DFM refinement already appeared in v1 Table 1; its fuller description does not establish a newly introduced component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet-1K class-conditional generation at 256×256 and class-conditioned inpainting, alongside the same illustrative categorical-sampling scenarios. The added sampler and caching studies change configurations within this coverage, without adding datasets, domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: The main comparison changes substantially: v1 Table 2's MDTv2 and MAR-H rows disappear, while v3 Table 1 adds SiT-XL, SiT-XL with Solver, and MaskGIL-XXL. This revises the continuous-model quality/efficiency comparison in particular. Appendix D also adds an explicit quantitative comparison against vanilla DFM sampling, previously discussed without a corresponding result curve.

E3.justification: v3 changes the component-ablation sequence, testing rehash sampling before adding 2D-RoPE/min-SNR. It adds matched-weight sampler-step sweeps and cache tests at 32/64 steps. Main evaluation settings remain largely unchanged. Table 4 introduces conflicting ablation settings—500k training steps and variable guidance versus Section 3.4/Table 3's 100k steps and constant guidance 2.0—so a consistent budget change or rerun cannot be inferred.

E4.justification: v1 Table 1(a)'s RepA presence/layer-position ablation is removed, and the general component ablation is revised. v3 adds a DFM/rehash/hybrid comparison across sampling steps in Figure 7 and cache speed-quality analysis in Table 5. These substantially change the evidence about component contributions and inference efficiency; the noise-capacity and timeline analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experimental comparisons. v3's cache-performance deltas are differences in reported scores, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The main ReDDiT gFID scores remain 2.13, 1.74 and 1.61, but the supporting results change substantially. v3 adds sampler-step curves and cache results, including XL-f8 gFID 1.71 at a reported 2.56× relative speed under caching. RepA-layer results disappear, baseline result entries change, and intermediate ablation values are revised, including the objective row from 6.25 to 6.23. These are added or revised results, not a headline same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Appendix C preserves the transition-matrix and reverse-process derivations already present in v1 Section 3.2, including their assumptions and case analysis. The explicit categorical-distribution notation, condensed main-text equations and proof headings clarify or relocate existing mathematics rather than introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The rehashing contribution and headline gFID reduction from 6.18 to 1.61 remain. The efficiency claim is narrowed: v1's abstract claims higher efficiency than continuous counterparts, whereas v3 drops that clause and Section 3.2 describes efficiency and performance as on par with continuous models.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies RepA as a convergence accelerator, stating that sufficiently long training eliminates its relative performance gain. It also qualifies the tokenizer-matched AR comparison by discussing representation alignment's incompatibility with unidirectional attention, and adds interpretations of partial DFM refinement and cache speed-quality tradeoffs.

D1.justification: Appendices D-F provide substantially more reproducibility information: detailed sampler pseudocode, architecture dimensions, learning rates, warmup, batch sizes, guidance ranges, training times and cache settings. Appendix E reports approximately 1.2× RepA training overhead. These mostly disclose previously unspecified details; Table 4's conflicting ablation settings remain a limitation. The abstract newly promises public code/models without supplying access instructions.

R1.justification: New citations cover SiT, differentiable solver search, MaskGIL, MMaDA and dLLM-Cache; the MAR and Variational Diffusion Models references disappear. The central positioning relative to masked visual token models, discrete diffusion and flow matching remains, with the existing related-work discussion relocated to Appendix B.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative: related work and detailed derivations move to appendices, the main methodology is condensed, and performance comparisons precede noise-capacity and ablation sections. Qualitative discussion is split into generation and editing, and new appendix sections organize sampler details, implementation, acceleration and disclosure material.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different title/header and citation layout. Figure 1 incorporates existing sample imagery, qualitative montages are recomposed or relocated, and plot labels are clarified. The ablation table gains separate training/sampling columns and loses its RepA panel. New Figure 7 and Tables 4-5 add sampler, configuration and acceleration displays.

improvement.justification: v3 improves inspectability through quantitative same-weight sampler comparisons and substantially fuller implementation documentation, while retaining the principal results. The net gain is limited: the RepA-layer ablation and MDTv2/MAR-H comparisons are removed, and Table 4 contradicts the main text about ablation training steps and guidance. The added evidence and documentation improve the paper, but these omissions and inconsistencies prevent a substantial overall improvement.
